speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you haven't provided the patient's specific symptoms or history yet. Please describe your current gait difficulties, any limb ataxia you experience, and your significant medical history so I can begin my evaluation.

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; could you tell me if you have a history of diabetes, hypertension, or any previous strokes? Additionally, have you noticed any weakness or numbness in your right arm or leg?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy.

I am concerned about your history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab, which is a known risk factor for PML. This condition often presents with subacute gait ataxia and limb incoordination. Please confirm if you have noticed any new visual changes, such as blind spots or double vision, in addition to your walking difficulties.
